texts.preamble: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Author: M.Satyanarayana Murthy Bench: M.Satyanarayana Murthy The Hon'Ble Sri Justice M.Satyanarayana Murthy Writ Petition Nos. 2259 And 2273 Of 2020 Common Order:
texts.facts: Both these writ petitions are filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by two different petitioners by names R. Venkateswarlu and P. Vasanth Reddy, questioning the orders of suspension of 2B License issued by the third respondent/The Deputy Commissioner of Prohibition & Excise, Ananthapuram in Rc.No.391/2019/C1 dated 27.01.2020, challenged in these two writ petitions on identical grounds and therefore, I find it expedient to decide both these writ petitions by common order. Since, the question involved in both these writ petitions is one and the same, W.P.No.2259 of 2020 is taken as leading case. The petitioner obtained Form-2B License to run Bar & Restaurant under the provisions of Andhra Pradesh (Grant of Licensee of Selling by Bar and Conditions of License) Rules, 2017 (for short 'The Rules, 2017'). Ever since the date of grant of license, the petitioner was conducting business in the name and style of Chandu Restaurant and Bar at Kadiri without contravening any of the provisions of the A.P. Excise Act, 1968 (for short 'The Act') and the Rules, 2017 framed therein. While the matter stood thus, the third respondent herein issued a show cause notice on 21.12.2019 alleging that the fourth respondent/Prohibition & Excise Superintendent submitted a report stating that the Station House Officer, Kadiri submitted a report stating that on 14.10.2019 at about 11:45 p.m (23:45 hrs), the Station House Officer, Kadiri along with staff conducted surprise inspection of the bar premises and collected two loose liquor bottles and checked the strength of the liquor and it was MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 found to be 26.4% and 25.4 up. The bottles were sent for chemical examination and the chemical analysis report shown as 26.0 and 26.7 and found that the liquor was diluted. Basing on the said report, the fourth respondent opined that the petitioner has willfully violated the provisions of Section 36(1)(b) & (c) of the Act r/w Rules 27, 33 and 37 of the Rules, 2017 and the third respondent directed the petitioner to submit explanation within seven (7) days from the date of receipt of the notice.
texts.arguments: As the offence alleged against the petitioner is purely technical in nature, the petitioner has not submitted any explanation within stipulated time and wanted to submit the explanation in the last week of the month and the same was not accepted on the ground that the period prescribed is already over. It is also further contended that, third respondent herein passed the impugned order suspending the P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/ 1 license, pending enquiry and that the action of the third respondent in suspending the license pending enquiry is not legal and the same is arbitrary; that the power to suspend the license is conferred on the third respondent under Section 31 of the Act. A reading of Section 31 of the Act, it is clear that the licensing authority is given the discretion to either suspend or cancel a license. It is submitted that the discretion has to be exercised by the third respondent taking into consideration, the seriousness of the allegations made against the licensee. A reading of the impugned order, it is clear that the only allegation against the petitioner is that the liquor strength is 26.4 and 25.4; that once the cap of the liquor bottle is opened, due to atmosphere condition also there would be a change in the strength of the liquor. The variation in the strength of the liquor by the manufacturer would be around 1 to 2 % and normally the change is not taken as a violation. MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 Similarly, the allegation made against the petitioner in W.P.No.2273 of 2020 is that, the strength of the liquor in respect of one bottle is 26.0 up instead of 24.9, the same is diluted in Indian made liquor. The specific contention of the petitioners in both the writ petitions is that, variation of liquor is very minimal and the third respondent without exercising the discretion conferred on it, mechanically passed the orders impugned in these writ petitions, pending enquiry. Hence, the orders are illegal, arbitrary and in violative of principles of natural justice. It is further contended that the orders passed by the third respondent is not disclosing any reason for suspension of the Bar License and it is contrary to the principle laid down by the Full Bench of this Court in Tappers Co-operative Society, Maddur v. Superintendent of Excise, Mahaboobnagar1, wherein this Court in paragraph 45 of the judgment held that the power of suspension, pending enquiry cannot be exercised in a routine manner and unless that the suspension is necessary. It is contended that the observations of the Full Bench are directly applicable to the facts of the case and on the strength of the principle laid down in the judgment referred supra, the petitioners specifically contended that the original Rules, 2017 were repealed by Rules, 2019. Therefore, the third respondent passed the order referring the Rules, 2017 and on this technical ground also, the impugned orders are liable to be set-aside. It is specifically contended that, Section 2(21) of the Act defines 'liquor' and it includes today. In so far as the Excise Act and the Bar 1984 (2) APLJ (HC) 1 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 Rules do not prescribe the procedure for collecting sample from the license premises. Rule 27 of the A.P. Excise (Grant of License to Sell Toddy, Conditions of License and Taping of Excise Trees) Rules, 2017 provide the procedure for drawl of samples. As per Rule 27 of the above Rules, three samples have to be collected and one sample should be kept with the license and one sample should be sent to the Court of competent jurisdiction and one sample should be sent for chemical examination. The said procedure is prescribed as adulteration of liquor would entail criminal consequences and the accused would be given an opportunity to request the authorities to send the second sample for chemical examination. In the present case, the authorities did not follow the Rules and have taken the entire bottle and sent the same for chemical examination. By reason of the same, the petitioner is deprived of an opportunity to seek sending the second sample for chemical examination. Hence, it is contended that the action of the respondents is illegal and arbitrary and the impugned orders are P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/ 2 liable to be set-aside on this ground alone. It is also contended that the petitioners have paid license fee and they are entitled for refund of the license fee for the period during which the petitioners have conducted business. It is further contended that the allegations made against these petitioners are nto so grave which warrant the order of suspension. Even the show cause notices issued by the third respondent fixing seven days time for submission of the explanation is contrary to the law laid down by the learned Single Judge of High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh2, where the High Court held that, 15 days time is reasonable time for 2013 (6) ALD 247 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 submitting an explanation from the date of service of notice. On this ground also, the petitioners requested to set-aside the impugned orders in these writ petitions. The respondents did not file any counter, but advanced arguments. During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioners Sri O. Manohar Reddy has drawn the attention of this Court to Rule 46 for lifting samples to contend that the person who lifted the samples is incompetent to lift the samples and therefore, the very lifting of samples is illegal, since it is in violation of the Rules, 2017. Even otherwise, as per Rule 27 of the A.P. Excise (Grant of License to Sell Toddy, Conditions of License and Taping of Excise Trees) Rules, 2017, three samples have to be collected and one sample should be kept with the license and one sample should be sent to the Court of competent jurisdiction and one sample should be sent to chemical examination. Instead of following such procedure, due to absence of any such Rule for lifting of samples of liquor in the bar, the fourth respondent adopted a short cut method and sent the entire bottle by lifting the sample, thereby the petitioners were deprived of their right to make application(s) for referring the samples to chemical examination. This amounts to denial of opportunity to prove their innocence, since adulteration of liquor leads to criminal prosecution having its serious consequences, involving issue of life and liberty. Even as per Food Adulteration Act, Food Inspector is entitled to lift the samples as per the Food Safety Standard Act, the Food Inspector is entitled to take samples following necessary procedure prescribed under the Act. Even they also can lift the samples from Bar & Restaurant, but they are required to follow the procedure MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 prescribed either under Food Adulteration Act, if the samples were drawn under the Food Adulteration Act and on account of repeal, the Food Inspector has to draw the samples by following the procedure prescribed under Food Safety Standard Act and Rules framed there under. If the samples were drawn by the Food Inspector, the petitioners will have an opportunity to prove their innocence by making a request to send the other sample handed over to the Court for chemical examination. But, on account of lack of sufficient clear procedure under the Rules, the petitioners are being suffered on account of suspension of license and therefore, requested to set-aside the same. Whereas, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Prohibition & Excise would contend that the petitioners were given an opportunity to submit their explanation within seven days, but they did not avail their opportunity and they cannot be prohibited to submit their explanation leisurely as and when they find time, on this ground alone, the request of the petitioners is liable to be rejected. P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/ 3 Yet, another contention raised by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Prohibition & Excise is that, when the Act is silent for granting specific time for submitting explanation to the show cause notice, the respondents are not expected to grant time to the satisfaction of the licensees and granting seven days time to submit explanation by the petitioners is in compliance of Section 31(1) of the Act and the same is in accordance with law and the same cannot be violated, consequently, on this ground of granting seven days time, the impugned orders cannot be set-aside. Yet another contention raised by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Prohibition & Excise is that the fourth respondent followed the procedure strictly, contemplated under the Rules, 2017 and absolutely there is no minor violation of the Rules, 2017, which vitiates the entire proceedings under challenge and requested to dismiss the writ petitions. But, the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that, atleast fifteen days time is required to be granted while calling for explanation of these petitioners in P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/ 4 exercise of power under proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act. The, learned counsel for the petitioners Sri O. Manohar Reddy contended that atleast 15 days time is to be granted before passing any order of suspension by relying on the judgment of the learned Single Judge of High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh3, where the High Court held that, 15 days time is reasonable time for submitting an explanation from the date of service of notice when an action is proposed to be taken either for suspension or cancellation. A similar issue was decided by the Division Bench of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh earlier, wherein it was held that an order of suspension passed without giving notice and opportunity to the licensee is illegal and liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. (vide. Sri Venkateshwara Wines v. Superintendent of Prohibition and Excise, Nizamabad and others4). No doubt, in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh case (referred supra), the learned Single Judge held that, 15 days time is reasonable time for submitting an explanation from the date of service of notice when an action is proposed to be taken either for suspension or cancellation. When once the seven 2004 (4) ALD 681 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 days notice was given to these petitioners contrary to the judgment in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh case (referred supra), it is an irregularity committed by the respondents in suspending Form-2B License of these petitioners by exercising power under Section 31(1) of the Act.
